comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) will replace and expand EU ESG reporting requirements starting in fiscal year 2024, with implementation delays in some member states, while the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) enacted in July 2024 mandates due diligence obligations for human rights and environmental impacts starting in 2027, impacting the Firm's EU and non-EU entities.
comparisons.comparison: While Goldman Sachs discloses its specific net-zero operational and financing targets, JPMorgan discusses the regulatory environment driving such sustainability efforts. GS explicitly states it has been 'carbon neutral in its operations and business travel since 2015' and aims to align financing activities with a 'net-zero-by-2050 pathway.' In contrast, JPM focuses on the implementation of the EU's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD), noting these require 'company-specific climate-related transition plans' and expand ESG reporting, but does not detail its own internal net-zero operational status or specific financing portfolio targets in this item.

sentences.text: With respect to Climate Transition, we have announced our goal to align our financing activities with a net-zero-by-2050 pathway.

We have been carbon neutral in our operations and business travel since 2015 through a combination of emissions reduction efforts and the procurement of Energy Attribute Certificates and third-party-verified carbon offsets.

The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive ("CSRD") will replace and significantly expand the scope and content of certain EU ESG reporting requirements, with phased-in requirements expected to start with fiscal year 2024.

The CSDDD sets mandatory due diligence obligations for companies to address actual and potential human rights violations and environmental adverse impacts stemming from their own operations and business relationships, including the activities of certain companies with which they have established business relationships and also requires the adoption of company-specific climate-related transition plans.
